name: White Gut Syndrome & White Feces Syndrome (WGS/WFS)
scientific_pathogen: Enterocytozoon hepatopenaei (EHP) microsporidian spores combined with opportunistic Vibrio parahaemolyticus and Vibrio alginolyticus
clinical_signs: White fecal strings floating on feeding trays and leeward pond surface
Empty gut with milky white, gelatinous transformation of the midgut
Soft shell, lethargy, reduced feed consumption by 40-70%
Severe size variation and stunted growth
banned_ineffective_treatments: Oxytetracycline, enrofloxacin, furazolidone (strictly banned by MPEDA/CAA; causes antimicrobial resistance and rejection of export consignments)

recommended_caa_protocol.manufacturer_location: New Autonagar, Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh, India
recommended_caa_protocol.active_consortium: Citrobacter freundii, Bacillus subtilis, Lactobacillus acidophilus, Saccharomyces cerevisiae
recommended_caa_protocol.feed_dosage: 15-20 ml per kg commercial pellet feed (two meals daily for 5-7 days)
recommended_caa_protocol.water_dosage: 1.0 - 2.0 Liters per acre water broadcast during early morning aeration

name: Toxic Total Ammonia Nitrogen (TAN) & Nitrite (NO2) Toxicosis
scientific_pathogen: Abiotic autotrophic nitrification collapse; accumulation of un-ionized NH3 and NO2-
clinical_signs: Shrimp gasping at water surface or congregating near aerators
Gill necrosis, red discoloration of pleopods and antennae
Loss of equilibrium and sudden post-feeding mortality spikes
Cyanosis and brown blood syndrome in finfish
banned_ineffective_treatments: Zeolite alone without biological nitrifiers (only binds trace cations temporarily; does not oxidize ammonia nitrogen)

recommended_caa_protocol.manufacturer_location: New Autonagar, Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh, India
recommended_caa_protocol.active_consortium: Autotrophic Nitrosomonas europaea, Nitrobacter winogradskyi, Paracoccus denitrificans
recommended_caa_protocol.water_dosage: 2.0 - 3.0 Liters per acre (1 meter depth) during active aerator operation

name: Luminescent Vibriosis & Red Disease (Acute Hepatopancreatic Necrosis)
scientific_pathogen: Vibrio harveyi, Vibrio parahaemolyticus, Vibrio vulnificus
clinical_signs: Green luminescence of shrimp body visible in dark night inspections
Reddish coloration of cephalothorax, pleopods, and uropods
Atrophied and melanized hepatopancreas
High mortality of 50-90% within 48-72 hours if untreated
banned_ineffective_treatments: Chlorine dioxide / bleaching powder overdosing (kills entire beneficial algae bloom, collapses pond dissolved oxygen, and triggers worse secondary Vibrio rebound)

recommended_caa_protocol.manufacturer_location: New Autonagar, Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh, India
recommended_caa_protocol.active_consortium: Bacillus subtilis (Subtilosin producing), Bacillus pumilus, Rhodococcus erythropolis
recommended_caa_protocol.water_dosage: 1.5 - 2.5 Liters per acre broadcast during early morning (8:00 AM)

name: Benthic Organic Sludge & Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S) Black Soil
scientific_pathogen: Anaerobic desulfurization bacteria (Desulfovibrio spp.) decomposing uneaten feed and dead plankton
clinical_signs: Rotten egg odor (H2S) emitted from check trays and drainage gates
Black staining on ventral abdominal segments, walking legs, and gill filaments
Shrimp avoiding pond bottom trenches, swimming along peripheries
Chronic low feed intake and tail rot
banned_ineffective_treatments: Potassium permanganate surface dosing (does not penetrate benthic organic mud layers)

recommended_caa_protocol.manufacturer_location: New Autonagar, Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh, India
recommended_caa_protocol.active_consortium: Thiobacillus denitrificans, Bacillus licheniformis, Bacillus megaterium, Protease & Cellulase enzyme complex
recommended_caa_protocol.water_dosage: 1 Can (5 Litres) per acre directly applied over central feeding trenches and dark sludge zones

name: Soft Shell Syndrome, Molting Cramps & Muscle Necrosis
scientific_pathogen: Abiotic ionic imbalance: Calcium (Ca2+), Magnesium (Mg2+), Potassium (K+) deficiency and low total alkalinity
clinical_signs: Thin, papery exoskeleton remaining soft > 24 hours post-molt
Opaque, white muscle necrosis in tail segments (cramped body)
Cannibalism during new moon and full moon molting peaks
High mortality during harvest and grading
banned_ineffective_treatments: Crude agricultural lime (slow solubility, spikes pH dangerously above 9.0 without bio-available ionic magnesium)

recommended_caa_protocol.manufacturer_location: New Autonagar, Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh, India
recommended_caa_protocol.active_consortium: Bio-chelated Calcium, Magnesium, Potassium, Zinc, Copper, Selenium, Vitamin D3 matrix
recommended_caa_protocol.water_dosage: 5 Litres per acre applied at night during aerated molting cycle
recommended_caa_protocol.feed_dosage: 10 ml per kg feed during new/full moon windows

name: Running Mortality Syndrome (RMS)
scientific_pathogen: Complex polymicrobial infection (Vibrio campbellii, toxic microalgae cyanotoxins, and environmental stress)
clinical_signs: Continuous daily mortality of 10-30 shrimp per pond between DOC 35 and DOC 70
Dead shrimp found with full gut or empty gut at feeding trays
Faded body pigmentation and cloudy muscle tissue
No single identifiable viral lesion on PCR screening

recommended_caa_protocol.water_dosage: 1 Can (5L) Next Converter + 2L Next Viro Nill per acre

name: Black Gill Disease & Branchial Melanization
scientific_pathogen: Fusarium solani fungal spores, chronic heavy silt/organic deposition, or chemical caustic burn
clinical_signs: Brownish to pitch-black discoloration of branchial gill filaments
Respiratory distress, shrimp swimming near pond surface and edge
Inability to tolerate routine salinity or oxygen fluctuations
Secondary bacterial colonisation by filamentous Leucothrix
banned_ineffective_treatments: Copper sulfate overdosing (causes severe gill lamellae fusion and acute toxicity)

Tail fan rigidity and spasmodic cramping during netting
Sudden mortality spikes 15-30 minutes after sampling
Secondary Vibrio invasion turning muscle tissue reddish-pink
